rv.q: It’s an early contender for the best performance of the year.
This show is a middle-brow beaut, the marriage of a timeless script and its near-perfect interpreter.
She gives an enormously sweet, touching and vulnerable performance that’s also joyful, powerful and eye-moistening.
The world really does feel like a brighter, more exciting place after a couple of hours in Valentine’s company.
Firing the gags right at the audience, Smith also evokes a note of sorrow at her 'unused life' I'd never felt before.
Smith, an ebullient performer who positively exudes warmth, has a ball with this one-woman play...
On the evidence of the performance I saw, which prompted a standing ovation, a star has been reborn.
And this is an expert revival, blessed with a true star performance, alive to every aspect of ‘Shirley Valentine’, from its big heart to its troubled soul.
The deeper, existential elements are powered by Smith’s disarming and quietly dazzling performance.
Good old Shirley certainly belongs in their exalted company.
It’s great to see her back on stage, even in material as dated as this.
Yet it just doesn’t feel like quite enough.
Shirley Valentine ranks with her very best work, which is saying something...
It is comic and hopeful and, in Smith’s gloriously vulnerable hands, sure to be a hit all over again.
This is a role she seems born to play.
And it’s a pleasure to see Smith back centre stage, once more casting her spell.
So it’s a real treat that her latest role puts her alone on stage for two whole hours – and what a divine time it is.
Her gift of instantaneous audience rapport combined with unimpeachable comic timing wrings every laugh from Russell's script that spins marital cliches into verbal gold.
The Scouse accent and comic timing are impeccable but what elevates the performance are the moments of mimicry when portraying the annoying people in Shirley’s life...

cn.t: Smith proves perfectly cast in Russell's 1986 monologue, delivering a warm, transcendent performance that overcomes the play's occasionally dated material. Critics largely charmed by her ability to connect with audiences in this crowd-pleasing revival.

vr.q: I give Shirley Valentine starring Sheridan Smith five stars
